text:
## Executive summary

Sprint 42 closed on plan. The team shipped both stretch deliverables (dashboard redesign and the new auth flow with magic link signup) and held cycle time below the team baseline across the sprint. Velocity landed at **67 story points**, beating the four sprint baseline of 58 by **16 percent**. Two onboarding empty state tickets carried over to Sprint 43 by design, both P3 priority.

## Highlights

- **Dashboard redesign shipped end to end.** Hero section, filter bar refactor, and the cohort retention chart all behind the new design system tokens.
- **Magic link auth flow shipped** with rate limiting, email copy review, and an abuse guard. Cycle time on the auth tickets averaged 4.2 days against a 4.5 day team baseline.
- **Light mode contrast audit closed.** Card footer contrast lifted from 2.37 to 6.4, no more WCAG AA misses.
- **Quality work landed** across two P2 backlog sweeps and a search index v2 filter spike.

## Watch list

- Marcus Johnson carried a lighter workload this sprint (3 tickets, 8 story points). Worth a one on one to check if context switching cost him capacity or if assignments missed him.
- Two onboarding empty state tickets (copy refresh, illustration swap) carry over to Sprint 43. Both P3, both blocked on design feedback that arrived at the end of week two.
- Junior engineer Kai Tanaka still tracking above the team cycle time baseline (5.6 days versus 4.5). Pair Kai with a senior on the W43 cohort heatmap work for a mentoring lift.

## Recommendations

- Extend the SDR AE pairing model from NAMER to EMEA in Sprint 43. The unit economics from the customer success retro support it, and the cohort retention work this sprint produced the data to back the move.
- Schedule a cycle time retrospective for the Sprint 43 retro slot. The sprint shaved 1.8 days off the team average across the two weeks. Worth documenting what changed so the gain holds.
- Move both onboarding empty state tickets to a single design pairing session early in Sprint 43 so they ship in week one rather than carrying again.

## Talking points

- **Both stretch deliverables shipped on plan.** Dashboard redesign plus magic link auth, no scope cuts.
- **Velocity beat the baseline by 16 percent** at 67 story points versus 58. Capacity headroom remained at 17 percent for unplanned work.
- **Cycle time improvement of 1.8 days** across the sprint, from 5.2 on day one to 3.4 on day fourteen.
- **Two carryover tickets are P3 onboarding polish** that depended on design feedback. Not a discipline issue.
- **Kai Tanaka pairing recommendation** for the cohort heatmap work in Sprint 43.
